observation: Drafts for refund emails state a 30-day refund window; the policy changed to 14 days, so agents rewrite the paragraph or stop using the assistant for refunds.
evidence: P01, P02 and P05 each described rewriting the refund paragraph in the last week (interviews). Enablement repeated it with a sample refund email and got the same outdated window.
ruled_out: Not training: the agents noticed the error themselves and know how to edit drafts. Not workflow: the assistant fits the reply step; the content is wrong.
next_check: Refund drafts state 14 days in a new sample of 10 refund emails.

observation: Account managers write renewal emails by hand; neither interviewee knew the assistant could start from the team's reply templates.
evidence: P07 and P08 both said they had not been shown the templates option and tried the assistant once, without templates (interviews, question 9).
ruled_out: Not tool: the templates option works when enablement shows it. Not habit: neither had seen the option, so the old way was the only way they knew.
next_check: After a 15-minute walkthrough on templates, both use the assistant for routine renewals.

observation: Call summaries are saved as a separate document, so reps copy each one into the CRM record by hand, and most stop using the assistant after a few calls.
evidence: P10, P11 and P12 described the copy step; the four reps who stopped give it as the reason (interviews). Usage log: 2 of 6 reps use it after the second week.
ruled_out: Not tool: the summaries are accurate and the save works. Not training: all three know how to use it; the extra step is what they avoid.
next_check: Summaries appear in the CRM record without a copy step, and the tracker row moves to regular.

observation: P04 uses the assistant for routine replies and writes complaint replies personally.
evidence: P04 said complaint replies need their own tone and judgment and that the assistant saves time on everything else (interview, section 3).
ruled_out: Checked whether P04 had tried it on complaints: they had, and chose not to. Nothing to fix.
